name: Hotel Teatro
insider_take: This historic gem sits in a beautifully restored 1911 building that once housed the Denver Tramway Building, blending old-world elegance with modern luxury in the heart of downtown.
whats_special: Hotel Teatro is housed in a stunning brick and terra cotta building designed by renowned architect Frank Edbrooke, who also created the iconic Brown Palace Hotel. The property features original architectural details like soaring ceilings, exposed brick walls, and vintage fixtures that transport guests back to Denver's golden age while offering contemporary amenities.
pro_tip: Request a room on the upper floors for spectacular views of the Rocky Mountains and downtown Denver skyline – the sunset views are particularly breathtaking from the west-facing rooms.
dont_miss: The hotel's prime location puts you steps away from the Denver Center for the Performing Arts (hence the "Teatro" name), Union Station's trendy shops and restaurants, and the 16th Street Mall. The on-site Restaurant Kevin Taylor offers award-winning cuisine in an intimate setting perfect for pre-theater dining.
pros: Historic theater-themed boutique hotel with unique architectural character
Prime downtown Denver location near arts district and cultural attractions
Elegant rooms featuring luxury amenities and sophisticated design
Exceptional dining at on-site restaurant with locally-inspired cuisine
cons: Historic building may have smaller room sizes typical of boutique properties
Urban location subject to typical downtown noise levels
